paragraphs: HydroPoint sells smart water management covering both indoor and outdoor use. That means round-the-clock water use analytics and leak detection alongside irrigation control. Two irrigation brands sit under the company: WeatherTRAK, for portfolio-wide remote management and visibility, and Baseline, which offers sensors and two-wire technology.

A third product, WaterCompass, provides real-time visibility into indoor water use. The company says its solutions typically deliver payback in as little as 24 to 36 months. It also claims benefits past the water bill, including reduced labor and operational costs and prevention of overwatering.

HydroPoint was founded in 2002 by technology entrepreneurs Chris Spain, Peter Carlson, and Chris Manchuck. In 2016 it expanded by acquiring Baseline Systems. One published case study reports that the City of Boise has seen up to 70% water savings on its Baseline sites compared with previous watering methods. Across its customers, the company reports saving over 27 billion gallons of onsite water and over $213 million in water costs in 2025.
